records.sample_scope: The public NFER assessment-hub page reports response percentages for a KS1 coin-value item; the retrieved page does not expose a full study methodology/sample-size description.
records.supports: Pupils can confuse coin value with perceptual/notation cues; the page reports 12% selecting a size-based distractor and 45% selecting a number-on-face distractor in the discussed item.
records.does_not_support: The exact prevalence of counting number of coins instead of total value, or a jurisdiction-wide prevalence estimate without the underlying assessment sample details.
records.use_note: Use together with NCETM/Oak guidance as support for probing coin value/unitising, not as a standalone prevalence study.

records.sample_scope: 22 primary pupils aged 9-11 completed 15 individual-interview tasks involving subtraction as difference across concrete, numeric and symbolic representations.
records.supports: Children vary in coordinating take-away and indirect-addition/difference interpretations of subtraction; flexible use of subtraction-as-difference is a meaningful reasoning construct.
records.does_not_support: A money-specific change misconception or prevalence of failing to link change with difference.
records.use_note: Use as broader direct mechanism evidence alongside money-specific NCETM guidance.

records.sample_scope: 27 Year 3/4 pupils in one Australian school completed a 69-item task-based interview; the paper also discusses Australian NAPLAN evidence on calendar/time problems.
records.supports: Primary pupils can have difficulty with calendar calculations and coordinating time units; Year 3/5 assessment evidence includes difficulties adding days/weeks/years to calendar dates.
records.does_not_support: The exact claim that pupils systematically assume every month has the same number of days.
records.use_note: Use as broader direct calendar/time evidence; keep the exact month-length wording as a diagnostic hypothesis unless a matching study is found.
